newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended up 2.6 percent, crossing back through the 900 point mark, as the return of some investors sparked technical buying, dealers said.
The AEX index of leading shares gained 23.06 points, or 2.58 percent, to end at 917.48. The index had opened down 14.36 points at 880.06.

The performance of the Dutch share market contrasted with that of most of its European rivals, although many did at least lift from their early losses. Some traders reasoned the Dutch market's gains today were a response to its sharp weakening on Friday.
"We were the most negative, so it's not a great surprise to see us as the most positive today," one trader said.
Traders said the strength of the dollar, which put on two guilder cents to 2.05 guilders, had also buoyed the Dutch market.
"Remember, we're one of the most dollar-sensitive of all European bourses," a trader said.

Few individual shares attracted attention in a day of low volumes, but traders commented they had seen fairly concerted buying of financial sector stock, partly in response to recent steady losses and partly in advance of figures due this week.
ABN AMRO, which reports half year figures on Thursday, put on 2.70 guilders to 47.00, while Aegon which follows with its half year results on Friday, added 4.70 guilders to 144.70.
Oil giant Royal Dutch which has slumped since early August, finished up 2.70 guilders, at 105.20. Its shares were the second most traded in the Dutch market.
"The financials and the likes of Royal Dutch were heavily sought today," one trader said.
